posts.quote: Dane County Borrows $25,000 For A Memorial Honoring A Man Who Pulled A Knife On Cops.
posts.alt: Photo from a Wisconsin DOJ released squad camera still of Madison police officers struggling with Corey Ruiz in the street at S. Baldwin St. as one officer points a Taser, with a circle inset of Ruiz's Wisconsin Department of Corrections photo. Text reads: Dane County Borrows $25,000 For A Memorial Honoring A Man Who Pulled A Knife On Cops. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credits: Wisconsin DOJ; Wisconsin Dept. of Corrections.
posts.caption:
Dane County is borrowing $25,000 to build a memorial at the corner where a man pulled a knife on Madison police.

His name was Corey Ruiz. He was 38.

On July 22, a homeowner called 911 about a man who had just tried to break into the house. An officer recognized Ruiz on the Ring video. Police chased him through the neighborhood. At Williamson and Baldwin he hit the pavement, fought officers, and pulled a knife. Two Tasers did not stop him. An officer fired three shots.

The DA's ruling: "Responding to that threat with deadly force is permitted under the law." No charges.

The county did not wait for that answer. The first $25,000 request was filed Sept. 1, more than two months before the DA ruled. It called his death an "officer-involved killing" and set up a county account named "COREY RUIZ MEMORIAL." That version got postponed. So it came back as an amendment to the 2027 capital budget, paid for with "BORROWING PROCEEDS." The board passed that budget Nov. 4, 27 to 10.

CNN reported Ruiz had pleaded guilty since 2021 to charges involving resisting police, including "battery or threat" to an officer. State records listed him as "absconded" from supervision.

The city has already burned an estimated $1 million, mostly police overtime, on the protests and the two-week street encampment that followed. The county resolution praised that encampment for offering "mutual aid."

A death is a tragedy for a family. But a monument built on borrowed public money at that corner tells every Madison cop who the county thinks the victim was.

"The permanent memorial is for all the victims of police killings in the neighborhood," Supervisor Yogesh Chawla said.

The officer who fired was hurt in that struggle. He gets an internal review. The man with the knife gets a monument.
posts.first:
The facts: Corey Ruiz, 38, was shot and killed by Madison Police Officer Kiel Baitinger-Peterson on July 22, 2026, at S. Baldwin and Williamson streets. The DA found "no potential criminal court liability" for officers on Nov. 19. The state DOJ said the officer was injured before he fired. Resolution 2026 RES-131 (filed Sept. 1) sought $25,000 and was postponed indefinitely by the Executive Committee on Sept. 24. Amendment EXEC-C-01 (Supervisors Chawla, Andrae, Erickson, Doolan) moved $25,000 in borrowing into the 2027 capital budget "to create a permanant memorial to victims of police killings" (county spelling). The Executive Committee approved it 4 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain. The board adopted the capital budget 27 to 10 on Nov. 4. The memorial will also honor Tony Robinson and Paul Heenan, killed by Madison police in 2015 and 2012.

Sources: Dane County DA release (Nov. 19), Dane County Legistar (2026 RES-131, 2026 RES-174 capital amendments and vote), WKOW, Cap Times, CNN, Wisconsin Examiner, WMTV, PBS Wisconsin, Wisconsin Right Now.
